item.title: Understanding the CURSORTRACE Event
item.description: The Oracle library cache is extensively instrumented, but the instrumentation is disabled by default. It can be enabled using the CURSORTRACE event, which is particularly useful for investigating library cache problems, especially cursor sharing issues related to child cursor mismatches, high version counts, or unexpected hard parses. Beyond troubleshooting, the CURSORTRACE event also provides valuable insights into the internal behavior of the library cache, as explored in this post (see also 1).
